request.initial_prompt: Hamlet. There's letters seal'd: and my two schoolfellows, Whom I will trust as I will adders fang'd,— They bear the mandate, they must sweep my way And marshal me to knavery. Let it work; For 'tis the sport to have the enginer Hoist with his own petard, and 't shall go hard But I will delve one yard below their mines And blow them at the moon. O, 'tis most sweet, When in one line two crafts directly meet. This man shall set me packing. I'll lug the guts into the neighbour room. Mother, good night. Indeed, this counsellor Is now most still, most secret, and most grave, Who was in life a foolish prating knave. Come, sir, to draw toward an end with you. Good night, mother.
